candidate.selection_reason: Extended placeholder regexp to include 'I' type -> allows injection of Infinity values during deserialization
candidate.source_summary: Infinity values from user-provided objects during serialization
candidate.sink_summary: eval() function in test suite that evaluates serialized output containing Infinity placeholders
candidate.guard_summary: No validation of Infinity values before serialization; unsafe eval() usage without sanitization
candidate.risk_pattern: Infinity values are serialized with '@__I-' placeholders and directly injected into eval() context without sanitization
candidate.context_summary: The regex change adds 'I' type for Infinity values. When serialized objects contain Infinity, they get placeholder tokens that are later replaced with raw Infinity values and evaluated with eval()
unresolved_facts: Whether the serialized output is used in production with eval() or only in tests
If there are any input validation mechanisms for Infinity values before serialization
Whether the eval() usage is limited to test environments only

target_cwe.description: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.
remediation_steps: Follow secure coding practices and security guidelines

stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: Stage-2 evidence shows serialization of user-provided Infinity values with placeholders that are later evaluated via eval() - matches deserialization vulnerability pattern
